name: Hazo
overview: Hazo is a male figure mentioned in the book of Genesis as the son of Nahor. There is no additional tribal affiliation or notable attributes recorded about him beyond his paternal lineage. Scripture provides limited information about Hazo, focusing primarily on his genealogical connection.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Hazo' is presented as a proper name in Genesis 22:22 without any specific meaning or divine attribution noted. It is simply recorded as his personal name without further explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Hazo is identified as a son of Nahor, making him part of the extended family of Abraham. He is also listed among the sons of Milcah, Nahor's wife, indicating his immediate family context. Beyond these relationships, Scripture does not provide further details about his family or descendants.
scriptureSignificance: Hazo's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his place within the genealogy of Nahor, Abraham's brother. His mention in Genesis 22:22 contributes to the broader understanding of Abraham's family lineage, which is foundational for tracing the covenantal promises God made to Abraham and his descendants. Though not a central character, Hazo's inclusion underscores the importance of family lines in God's unfolding plan.
